item.title: Nor'easter brings heavy flooding, major power outages to the East Coast
item.description: Tens of millions of people are in the path of the storm, which has canceled flights, concerts and sporting events.

item.title: Hurricane Nolo could cause "catastrophic" flooding in Hawaii, forecasters warn
item.description: Hurricane Nolo weakened slightly as it began to move away from Hawaii, forecasters said, but it was still expected to lash the Big Island and Maui with heavy rains through the weekend.

item.title: Trump rejects 7-day plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran had presented a seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and return to negotiations for a lasting end to the war.

item.title: How playing Mahjong could improve your brain health later in life
item.description: Mahjong is having a moment, drawing a new generation of fans who are joining clubs and getting into the game. And a growing body of research suggests it could benefit your brain later in life. Bradley Blackburn explains.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Sept. 27)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Suicide survivor shares mission to help others as new research reveals power of small joys
item.description: New research is shedding light on suicide prevention and possible techniques to help people in crisis. During this suicide prevention awareness month, Natalie Brand spoke to a survivor on a mission to help others.

item.title: Russian foreign minister accuses Europe of blocking Ukraine peace talks
item.description: Both Moscow and Kyiv have stepped up attacks after the deadliest summer since 2022 — the year Russia launched its invasion of Ukraine.

item.title: From red and blue to black and silver: Why America's cars have lost their color
item.description: If you take a look around on the road these days, you may notice cars seem a lot less colorful. Bright blues, reds, and yellows have increasingly given way to black, white, and silver. CBS News' Evyn Moon looks at why America's cars have lost their color.

item.title: Massive crowd of worshippers in France attend Mass during Pope Leo visit
item.description: The Vatican estimated that 800,000 people came out for the Mass.

item.title: Trump and Xi to set up AI safety channel as military, trade talks continue
item.description: The White House said the two leaders agreed on using the term "super intelligence" rather than "artificial intelligence" to describe the technology.

item.title: 4 American tourists dead after building explosion in Greece
item.description: The mayor of Athens said the explosion was likely caused by a gas leak.

item.title: Hurricane Polo is a strong Category 4 storm off Mexico. See its path.
item.description: Hurricane Polo was downgraded to Category 4 status Saturday as its intensity fluctuated off Mexico's southwestern coast. The storm is expected to slowly weaken over the weekend, the hurricane center said.

item.title: Fears of serial killer rise in South Africa after body of 10th woman found
item.description: Police have identified similarities in some of the killings but said they had not found conclusive evidence that the same person or people were responsible.

item.title: Iranian President Pezeshkian talks about proposal to reopen Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran's Masoud Pezeshkian, who is also a physician, says he has visited Iran's supreme leader twice and talked with CBS News' Margaret Brennan about Mojtaba Khamenei's health.

item.title: Saturday Sessions: Karina Rykman performs "Shoegaze Summer"
item.description: New York City native Karina Rykman has earned accolades for her unmissable live act. The singer-songwriter and bassist recently celebrated the release of her new studio album, "Late Checkout," at Zabar's, becoming the first band to play at the iconic Upper West Side delicatessen. Here's Karina Rykman with "Shoegaze Summer."

item.description: Some units would "possibly [be] needed in 90-120 days," according to an internal Army message reviewed by CBS News.

item.description: Comedian Stavros Halkias speaks with Nate Burleson about his latest standup special, his hit show "Tires," his role in the Anthony Bourdain biopic, "Tony," and more.

item.title: Highlights magazine celebrates 80 years
item.description: For decades, children have sent Highlights magazine their drawings, poems, questions and concerns. Now Highlights is turning 80. We took a look back at the beloved magazine's history.

item.title: FAA rolls out new AI flight software
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration is rolling out new air traffic control software that uses artificial intelligence as a prediction tool. This comes as more than half of Americans worry that AI models could act on their own to cause harm, accord to a CBS News survey. Kris Van Cleave has the story.

item.description: A nor'easter is dumping rain on parts of the East Coast while Hurricane Nolo stalls off the coast of Hawaii's Big Island. "CBS Saturday Morning" has team coverage.

item.title: The story behind the first CIA officers in Afghanistan after 9/11
item.description: Twenty-five years ago, a Soviet-designed helicopter crossed the mountains of Afghanistan with the first CIA officers sent into the country after 9/11, the opening move in what would later become America's longest war.

item.title: OpenAI agent accessed government website data after going rogue, company reveals
item.description: The disclosure comes at a time of heightened concern over AI agents acting outside of human control.

item.title: Trump cancels nearly $1 billion in spending, a move some lawmakers called illegal
item.description: President Trump moved to cancel almost $1 billion in spending that was approved by Congress, marking the second time his administration has employed a rarely used tactic that some lawmakers in both parties have called illegal.
